title: Koszul and finite-quotient completion are canonically identified, preserving the units; their common functor is the reflector for the local internal-H
statement:
Let \(\mathcal C\) be a small category with Grothendieck topology \(J\), let \(A\) be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let \(I\subseteq A\) be an ideal. Let \(\underline A\) be the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], put \(S_n=\underline{A/I^{n+1}}\), and let \(B=\varprojlim_n S_n\) with its quotient projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit, def-sfb-constant-completion-coefficient-data]. For \(b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\), let \(\mathcal O_b\) be \(\underline A\) when \(b=\mathrm{false}\) and \(B\) when \(b=\mathrm{true}\); write \(\operatorname{coefficients}(J,A,I,b)=\mathcal O_b\), \(\operatorname{finiteMap}(J,A,I,b,n):\mathcal O_b\to S_n\), and \(\operatorname{completion}(J,A,I,b)\) with unit \(\operatorname{completionUnit}(J,A,I,b)\) for the normalized strict quotient-tower completion data [def-pur-strict-quotient-completion-data, def-sfb-constant-completion-coefficient-data]. Use the standard unbounded derived category \(D(\mathcal O_b)\) of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let \(\operatorname{IsComplete}(q,M)\) denote local derived completeness for the kernel of a ring-sheaf quotient \(q\) [def-sfb-quotient-kernel-completeness].

Let \(r\geq0\), let \(a:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A\) (allowing the empty list), and assume \(\operatorname{Ideal.span}(\operatorname{Set.range}a)=I\). Let \(\operatorname{KoszulPresentation}(J,A,I,b,r,a)\) be the strict derived Koszul-limit presentation for \(\mathcal O_b\) and the images of the entries of \(a\), and write \(\operatorname{koszulCompletion}(J,A,I,K)\) and \(\operatorname{koszulUnit}(J,A,I,K,-)\) for its completion functor and normalized unit [def-sf-constant-coefficient-koszul-completion-data]. Then there exist a presentation \(K:\operatorname{KoszulPresentation}(J,A,I,b,r,a)\) and an isomorphism of functors
\[
e:\operatorname{koszulCompletion}(J,A,I,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{completion}(J,A,I,b)
\]
such that, for every \(M\in D(\mathcal O_b)\),
\[
\operatorname{koszulUnit}(J,A,I,K,M)\,;\,e_M=\operatorname{completionUnit}(J,A,I,b)_M.
\]
Moreover, every \(\operatorname{completion}(J,A,I,b)(M)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{IsComplete}(\operatorname{finiteMap}(J,A,I,b,0),\operatorname{completion}(J,A,I,b)(M))\). If \(L\) satisfies \(\operatorname{IsComplete}(\operatorname{finiteMap}(J,A,I,b,0),L)\), precomposition with the completion unit is a bijection
\[
\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{completion}(J,A,I,b)(M),L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(M,L).
\]
For every \(M\), the completion unit is an isomorphism if and only if \(\operatorname{IsComplete}(\operatorname{finiteMap}(J,A,I,b,0),M)\).

proof.text: On the constant coefficient sheaf, the Noetherian hypothesis and ha identify the ideal generated by the images of a with I. The finite Koszul augmentation to the quotient tower therefore has a pro-zero cone in the derived category: every level is killed by a sufficiently far transition. This applies also for r=0, when both towers are constant and the cone is zero.

proof.text: Apply exact constant sheafification followed by the flat scalar extension along \(\underline A\to\mathcal O_b\) to the pro-zero cone of Step 2. For b=false this map is the identity; for b=true the constant-completion equivalence states that \(B\) is flat over \(\underline A\) and that the projections induce \(B/I^{n+1}B\cong\underline{A/I^{n+1}}=S_n\), so \(\mathcal O_b\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{A/I^{n+1}}\cong S_n\) and \(\mathcal O_b\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{Q_{n+1}(A)}\) is the strict Koszul tower of the images of a (reindexing the Koszul exponent n+1 against the quotient index n). The flat-constant-tensor pro-zero lemma, applied with \(R=\underline A\to\mathcal O_b\), says that tensoring by any K-flat model P preserves pro-zero cones, induces an isomorphism on total right derived inverse limits, and carries the compatible augmentation maps P→Rlim to each other. Thus the strict Koszul and finite-quotient towers have canonically isomorphic derived-limit objects, compatibly with the units, over either coefficient sheaf coefficients J A I false or coefficients J A I true.

proof.text: The strict-tower derived-limit comparison identifies the derived limit of the finite reductions with the normalized total right derived inverse limit, and carries the Koszul augmentation to the quotient completion unit. The constant-completion equivalence records this identification for both the constant and completed coefficient sheaves, with the finite transition maps respected. Hence there is an isomorphism e : koszulCompletion J A I K ≅ completion J A I b satisfying koszulUnit J A I K M ≫ e.hom.app M = (completionUnit J A I b).app M for every M.

proof.text: For the completed branch, apply the constant-completion equivalence directly. It identifies restriction along the canonical map from the constant sheaf to B with an equivalence of complete derived subcategories, and its finite-reduction comparison identifies the Koszul and quotient derived limits while respecting their units. Thus the same unit-preserving e exists for b=true; exact restriction is conservative, so the augmentation isomorphism and completeness criterion transport from the constant branch.

proof.text: The ringed Koszul reflector gives, for every locally complete L, a bijection by precomposition with koszulUnit. Conjugating this bijection by e gives the displayed bijection by precomposition with completionUnit. At n=0, the kernel of finiteMap is I times O_b: for b=false this is the sheafification of the quotient kernel, and for b=true the canonical isomorphism B/IB isomorphic to the constant sheaf A/I from the constant-completion equivalence identifies the kernel with I times B. By the definition of IsComplete for a quotient kernel, this is exactly the local completeness predicate. Taking L=completion(M) gives the unit-isomorphism criterion; naturality and uniqueness follow from injectivity of the Hom bijections.

lean.statement:
theorem koszul_quotient_reflector [IsNoetherianRing A] (b : Bool) (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A)
    (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = I) :
    ∃ K : KoszulPresentation J A I b r a,
      (∃ e : koszulCompletion J A I K ≅ completion J A I b,
        ∀ M : D (coefficients J A I b), koszulUnit J A I K M ≫ e.hom.app M =
          (completionUnit J A I b).app M) ∧
      (∀ M : D (coefficients J A I b),
        IsComplete (finiteMap J A I b 0) ((completion J A I b).obj M)) ∧
      (∀ (M L : D (coefficients J A I b)), IsComplete (finiteMap J A I b 0) L →
        Function.Bijective (fun f : (completion J A I b).obj M ⟶ L ↦
          (completionUnit J A I b).app M ≫ f)) ∧
      (∀ M : D (coefficients J A I b),
        IsIso ((completionUnit J A I b).app M) ↔ IsComplete (finiteMap J A I b 0) M) := by
  sorry
